title: Content vs. Form: What Drives the Writing Score Gap Across Socioeconomic Backgrounds? A Generated Panel Approach

bias_targets.methodology: Decomposing the writing score gap between high- and low-SES (socioeconomic status) students into content, style, and scoring-function components by generating controlled stylistic rewrites of essays using LLMs and evaluating them with predictive scoring models.

Applying the LLM-based generated panel approach and Kitagawa-Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition to measure and separate the components (content vs. style) of writing score gaps between White and non-White students.
Utilizing the LLM-generated essay rewrites and predictive scoring models to decompose the observed writing score gaps between male and female students.
